title: Integrated Biometrics System/Facial Recognition
description: This RFI is issued in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.201. DoS is conducting market research pursuant to FAR Part 10 to identify qualified and experienced businesses capable of providing a COTS (Commercial Off-the-Shelf) solution with a secure, scalable, and high performing facial recognition capabilities that integrate with existing enterprise systems and workflows while supporting operational efficiency, mission effectiveness, and evolving security requirements. Please see attached RFI and PWS for additional details. RFI Responses need to be submitted by Friday, December 11, 2026 to the following: Padmavathi Washington-Sicher - Washington-sicherp@state.gov Felicia Goudy - GoudfyFD@state.gov NO PHONE CALLS, thank you.

title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) - MULTI-CHANNEL MANPACK (MCMP) RADIO CAPABILITY - AMENDMENT 01
description: AMENDMENT 01 The purpose of this amendment is to reconcile administrative inconsistencies in the solicitation number across the RFI documentation and provide a revised Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) attachment. 1. Solicitation Number Clarification: The official RFI number is and remains M67854-27-I-2001. Any prior references within the posting or documentation citing M67854-26-2001 were clerical errors and are hereby corrected. 2. Attachment Replacement: Added: Attachment 1 - NDA (Revised 11.10.2026) (updated to reflect the correct RFI number: M67854-27-I-2001). Action Required: Interested parties must execute and submit the updated file, "Attachment 1 - NDA (Revised 11.10.2026)," with their response packages. Submissions utilizing previous versions of Attachment 1 will not be accepted. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) MULTI-CHANNEL MANPACK (MCMP) RADIO CAPABILITY M67854-27-I-2001 1.0 GENERAL INFORMATION Document Type: Request for Information/Market Research Sources Sought: All Businesses � Under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code 334220 Closing date for RFI: 11 December 2026 at 1600 PM EST This RFI is for informational and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation for bids or proposals and is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government. No Statement of Work or Performance Specifications is currently available for release. The technical requirements package for this RFI is contained in the Controlled Attachment titled "MCMP System Requirements," which contains Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI). Access to this attachment is restricted and must be requested separately on SAM.gov in accordance with the procedures outlined in Section 4.0. This RFI is a market research tool to determine the availability and adequacy of potential commercial sources. The Government is not obligated to reimburse, and will not pay, for any information received from potential sources as a result of this RFI. The information provided herein is subject to change and in no way binds the Government to solicit for, or award, a competitive or sole source contract. 2.0 DESCRIPTION The Portfolio Acquisition Executive � Marine Corps (PAE-MC) Program Manager Tactical Communications and Electromagnetic Warfare Systems (PM TCE), Product Manager Tactical Radios (PdM TR), Ground Radios (GR) team is seeking industry feedback regarding a Multi-Channel ManPack (MCMP) Radio capability. The Marine Corps seeks Commercial or Non-Developmental Items (NDI) that can meet Marine Corps operational requirements. The purpose of this RFI is to aid in the requirements generation process and to seek feedback from industry on the status of potential replacements. This RFI is being issued to all available and qualifying vendors to collect information regarding industry capabilities to provide all listed items as an entire system. 3.0 BACKGROUND The Marine Corps seeks a Commercial or NDI solution that meets National Security Agency (NSA) High-Assurance Communications Security (COMSEC) modernization requirements and possesses improved size, weight, and power (SWaP) attributes. The MCMP will be configured in both a mounted (track and wheeled vehicles) and dismounted configuration. Radios will be networkable, enabling command and control at the lowest tactical level. The MCMP will leverage commercially available or non-developmental solutions to rapidly meet operational requirements. However,the Government is primarily interested in technologies currently exhibiting a Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of 8 or greater to support rapid fielding timelines. 4.0 ACCESS TO CUI ATTACHMENTS (MCMP SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS) The technical specifications outlining the mandatory system capabilities for this effort are contained in the Controlled Attachment titled "MCMP System Requirements". This file contains Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and/or Federal Contract Information (FCI). In accordance with federal security regulations and Department of War (DoW) information security policies, this document is locked to the public on SAM.gov. Interested parties must request access to this document separately on SAM.gov and satisfy the security requirements detailed below. MANDATORY SAM.GOV ACCOUNT SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS Before submitting an access request, your organization must ensure your SAM.gov account is configured correctly: Required Account Roles: The individual user submitting the access request on SAM.gov MUST have been assigned either the "Administrator" or "Data Entry" role in the Contract Opportunities domain for your registered entity. Troubleshooting: If you do not have one of these two roles assigned to your profile, the "Request Access" button will be inactive. The Government contracting office cannot manage, assign, or edit user roles within your company's SAM.gov profile. Please contact your company's internal SAM.gov Entity Administrator to update your permissions. MANDATORY SECURITY AND COMPLIANCE REQUIREMENTS To receive approval to view the "MCMP System Requirements" attachment, vendors must satisfy all of the following requirements: Active SAM.gov Registration: The entity's registration must be active and complete. Executed Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA): A signed copy of the Government-furnished "MCMP Project Non-Disclosure Agreement" (attached publicly to this announcement as Attachment 1 - NDA (Revised 11.10.2026)). And one of the following: Active DD Form 2345 (JCP): Your company must hold an approved DD Form 2345 with the Joint Certification Program (JCP) through the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA). SPRS NIST SP 800-171 Score: A current self-assessment score must be posted in the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS). Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Level 2: A current CMMC Level 2 self-assessment or CMMC third-party assessment. INSTRUCTIONS TO REQUEST ACCESS To request access to the "MCMP System Requirements" attachment: Log into SAM.gov with your credentialed account, navigate to this opportunity notice, locate the "MCMP System Requirements" attachment, and click "Request Access." In the justification text box provided by SAM.gov, you MUST input your company's Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code and Unique Entity ID (UEI). Requests lacking a CAGE code will be rejected. Download Attachment 1 - NDA (Revised 11.10.2026) (MCMP Project Non-Disclosure Agreement) from the public attachments section of this notice. Complete, sign, and date the agreement. Send a companion verification email to Hyung Lee, hyung.lee@usmc.mil, with a courtesy copy to Wanda Harner, wanda.harner@usmc.mil. Use the subject line: `MCMP RFI CUI Access Request - [Company Name] - CAGE: [XXXXX]`. Attach to the email: (1) Your executed MCMP Project NDA, AND (2) ONE of the following verifying documents: A copy of your active DD Form 2345 (JCP), OR Proof/screenshot of your posted SPRS score, OR Proof of your current CMMC Level 2 certification. 5.0 RESPONSE FORMAT Responses should be prepared in accordance with the following guidelines: Utilizing either Word (docx, 2013 or newer) or Adobe (.pdf) software. Times New Roman 12 (or larger) font, single-spaced, including tables, on 8.5 by 11 inches paper. A font size smaller than 12 may be used in figures and drawings, but type shall be clearly legible. Margins on all sides (top, bottom, left, and right) shall be at least 1 inch. A cover sheet that includes: Project title. Company name. Product name(s) Primary point of contact, including name, address, phone and e-mail contact information; and Date of submission. Interested parties are requested to provide an information package addressing their approach to meeting the Mandatory Requirements listed above, to include the following: Your organization�s description of, and its capability to provide, an integrated solution which meets the requirements defined in this RFI. Please provide details concerning integration efforts as well as components to be used. A description

title: Greece – Waste and rubbish containers and bins – ΠΡΟΜΗΘΕΙΑ ΚΑΔΩΝ ΑΠΟΡΡΙΜΜΑΤΩΝ
description: Αντικείμενο της σύμβασης είναι η προμήθεια κάδων απορριμμάτων (σύμμεικτων), κατάλληλων για την αποκομιδή των αστικών αποβλήτων, για την κάλυψη των αναγκών καθαριότητας του Δήμου Φυλής για τα έτη 2027-2028. Η σύμβαση αφορά την προμήθεια τροχήλατων κάδων και ειδικότερα την προμήθεια χιλίων διακοσίων (1.200) πλαστικών κάδων απορριμμάτων χρώματος πράσινου, ενδεικτικής χωρητικότητας 1.100 λίτρων, κατάλληλων για την μηχανική αποκομιδή των σύμμεικτων απορριμμάτων και εκατό (100) μεταλλικών κάδων απορριμμάτων, ενδεικτικής χωρητικότητας 1.100 λίτρων, κατάλληλων για την μηχανική αποκομιδή των σύμμεικτων απορριμμάτων. Η δαπάνη για τη συγκεκριμένη προμήθεια προϋπολογίζεται να ανέλθει στις 395.560,00€ συμπεριλαμβανομένου ΦΠΑ (Προϋπολογισμός χωρίς ΦΠΑ 319.000,00€ και ΦΠΑ 24% 76.560,00€) και θα καλυφθεί με χρηματοδότηση από ιδίους πόρους που θα βαρύνει ισόποσα τον προϋπολογισμό του Δήμου του οικονομικού έτους 2027 με το ποσό των 197.780,00€ και το 2028 με το ποσό των 197.780,00€ και ειδικότερα τον ΑΛΕ 020.3120903001. Οι τιμές μονάδας που αναγράφονται στον ενδεικτικό προϋπολογισμό της μελέτης της Υπηρεσίας, εκτιμήθηκαν με βάση την έρευνα αγοράς από το ελεύθερο εμπόριο. Η προμήθεια κατατάσσεται στους Κωδικούς Κοινού Λεξιλογίου δημοσίων συμβάσεων (CPV): 34928480-6 (Δοχεία και κάδοι απορριμμάτων). Η εκτέλεση της παραπάνω προμήθειας θα γίνει με την διενέργεια δημόσιου ηλεκτρονικού διαγωνισμού άνω των ορίων και με κριτήριο κατακύρωσης την πλέον συμφέρουσα από οικονομική άποψη προσφοράς, βάσει τιμής σύμφωνα με τις διατάξεις του Ν.4412/2016 όπως τροποποιήθηκαν και ισχύουν, για το σύνολο των προς προμήθεια ειδών. Η παρούσα σύμβαση δεν υποδιαιρείται σε τμήματα (ομάδες). Προσφορές υποβάλλονται για το σύνολο των παραπάνω ειδών. Η διάρκεια υλοποίησης της προμήθειας ορίζεται στα δυο (2) έτη από την ημερομηνία υπογραφής της σύμβασης, και το αργότερο μέχρι 31/12/2028 ή έως την εξάντληση του ποσού και των ποσοτήτων. Η σύμβαση μπορεί να τροποποιείται κατά τη διάρκειά της, χωρίς να απαιτείται νέα διαδικασία σύναψης σύμβασης, μόνο σύμφωνα με τους όρους και τις προϋποθέσεις του άρθρου 132 του ν. 4412/2016 και κατόπιν γνωμοδότησης της καθ’ ύλην αρμόδιας υπηρεσίας ή άλλως της υπηρεσίας η οποία ορίζεται με απόφαση της Α.Α. Αναλυτική περιγραφή του φυσικού και οικονομικού αντικειμένου της σύμβασης δίδεται στην υπ’ αριθμ. 16/2026 μελέτη της Δ/νσης Καθαριότητας & Ανακύκλωσης και στο ΠΑΡΑΡΤΗΜΑ Ι της παρούσας διακήρυξης.

title: Justice Command Center Phase II Renovation - RFI
description: Disclaimer: This notice is for informational purposes only. This is not a request for proposal or quote. It does not constitute a solicitation and shall not be construed as a commitment by the government or a guarantee that one will be issued in the future. Responses in any form are not offers and the government is under no obligation to award a contract as a result of this announcement. No funds are available to pay for preparation of responses to this announcement. Any information submitted by respondents is strictly voluntary. The Department of Justice (Department or DOJ), Security and Emergency Planning Staff (SEPS) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to seek information regarding industry capabilities to provide modernization and enhancements to a 24/7 crisis management and communications center. Vendors should provide details on enhancing capabilities into a modern state-of-the-art facility suitable for executive level staff and their guests and increasing situational awareness capabilities. Vendors should also provide details on services they can provide for 24/7 operational centers. The DOJ is reviewing the marketplace to proactively examine all available options to ensure that the Department�s technology investments deliver maximum value, flexibility, and innovation today, and into the future. Project Name: Justice Command Center Phase II Renovation Background: The Justice Command Center (JCC) is a secure 24-hour facility operating in support of law enforcement and national security programs. The JCC is the primary information gathering and crisis management facility for the Attorney General (AG) and senior Department officials; it is designed to function during routine operations and emergencies. The last renovations to the JCC were in 2006 and consisted of minor cosmetic improvements. The JCC needs major renovations to continue to provide the best service possible to the Departmental leadership. Objectives: The Department of Justice Command Center modernization encompasses the renovation and upgrade of the JCC suite, which currently comprises three (3) conference rooms, one (1) watch floor, two (2) IT server rooms, two (2) restrooms, and one (1) storage room. The renovation shall deliver the following enhancements: upgrades to existing conference rooms to modern standards suitable for executive-level meetings and high-level briefings, modern design elements and finishes, renovation of the watch floor to support advanced situational awareness and real-time operational collaboration, and upgrades to all common areas and support spaces to contemporary standards while maintaining compliance with all security and operational requirements. Upon completion, the renovations shall provide a modern environment that is suitable for executive level staff and supports the JCC�s mission as the primary information gathering and crisis management center for senior Department officials. Miscellaneous Requirements: Security: 1. Contractors must be able to pass National Crime Information Center (NCIC) background check for building access. The JCC is a Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF), therefore no devices with Wi-Fi or Bluetooth, photography, and/or recording capabilities are permitted within the JCC. 2. All visitors to the Restricted Area build site will be escorted/monitored by cleared personnel. Availability: The JCC is a 24/7 operation; however, work should be done after normal business hours (1800 � 0600) to limit disruptions to Department leadership. Compliance: 1. Intelligence Community Directive (ICD) 705; 2. ICD 705-1 Technical Specifications; and 3. TEMPEST Countermeasures. Tasks: Room 1: 1. Executive level conference table with DOJ seal engraved in center of the table 2. Enhanced appearance with new drywall, fresh paint, and decor; and 3. New desk to match conference room table with enough space for four (4); and enclaves, one (1) keyboard, one (1) mouse, two (2) monitors, and one (1) KVM; and 4. Unclassified Telephone Security Group (TSG) 6 approved speaker phone 5. Hidden but easily accessible cable raceway; and 6. New executive level furniture to include credenza,, and end tables; and 7. TotalMass MassLoaded Vinyl (MLV) Barrier (sounds dampening material which meets Sound Transmission Class (STC) 50 sound attenuation requirements); and 8. Replace existing carpet with new carpet tiles (unique to AG Conference Room space) Room 2: 1. Modernized appearance with new drywall, fresh paint, and updated decorative lighting (sconces); and 2. Updated Department of Justice and/or Justice Command Center Wall Signage; and 3. Dedicated workspaces (2) which allow for up to four (4) enclaves, one (1) keyboard, one (1) mouse, two (2) monitors, and one (1) KVM; and 4. Additional seating along walls; and 5. New podium (reduced size to accommodate video wall) with three (3) JCON enclaves; and 6. TotalMass MLV Barrier (sounds dampening material which meets STC-50 sound attenuation requirements). Room 3: 1. Executive level conference table for up to six (6) people; and 2. New 60� credenza to accommodate IT equipment and wiring; and 3. One (1) desk with three (3) enclaves; and 4. Executive level chairs; and 5. Enhanced appearance with new drywall and fresh paint; and 6. Match carpet tiles to existing floor in the JCC suite; and 7. New LED lighting and ceiling tiles; and 8. Two 75� 4k LED monitors. Room 4: 1. Collaborative layout desks for the Watch Officers; and 2. Dedicated workspace for the Lead Emergency Actions Specialist and Lead Telecommunication Specialist within the watch floor (Two Leads, Two Watch Officers); and 3. New 24/7 high durability desk chairs (5 chairs total); and 4. Printer Cove with three (3) printers (GFE); and 5. Built-in cabinetry for storage and binders; and 6. Additional desk for shared IT equipment (GFE) (LMR Radio, WashFax, Desktop VTC etc.); and 7. Zoned LED lighting with dimmer switch(s) compatible with watch environment; and 8. Hidden but easily accessible cable raceway; and 9. Dry Erase Magnetic Glass Board for planning; and 10. Privacy Smart Glass window between the Watch Room and the Situation Room 11. Adjustable temperature control for HVAC; and 12. Black 2x2 ceiling tiles; and 13. Remove or lower the existing raised floor for ADA compliance; and 14. New DOJ and/or JCC Signage; and 15. Six (6) Belkin 4:2 Display Port MultiClave Secure KVM. JCC Lobby/Reception Area (Modernized Design and Functionality): 1. Fresh paint; and 2. Additional seating; and 3. Improved LED signage throughout JCC; and 4. New Department of Justice Signage outside SCIF; and 5. New artwork throughout JCC; and 6. Recessed cell phone lockers outside of the SCIF. Modernizing the JCC into a state-of-the-art communications and meeting hub will provide Cabinet-level officials and senior managers with a secure, resilient, and highly adaptable environment for decision-making, collaboration, and organizational coordination. The existing space can be transformed from a primarily operational command function into a multi-functional executive hub capable of supporting high-level meetings, crisis response, strategic communications, and hybrid collaboration. The proposed enhancements will also allow the Watch Officers to have increased situational awareness during rapidly evolving emergency events, therefore creating additional information sharing opportunities with the Department�s senior leadership. title: Request for Information (RFI)- Parallel Battery Relay
description: 1. NOTICE This Request for Information (RFI) is issued for informational and market research purposes only in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10. It does not constitute a solicitation, a Request for Proposal (RFP), or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. The Government will not reimburse any company or individual for expenses associated with preparing or submitting information in response to this RFI. The information provided may be used by the U.S. Air Force in developing its acquisition strategy, Statement of Work (SOW), and performance specifications. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary or competition-sensitive information. 2. BACKGROUND AND SCOPE The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC), MH-139A Program Office (AFLCMC/WIH), is conducting market research to identify sources capable of providing Parallel Battery Relay modification for the MH-139A. The MH-139A missions routinely require off-station engine starts using only battery power. Flight data indicates that isolated battery starts in extreme cold weather degrade transient voltage, resulting in failed or hot engine starts. The objective of this effort is to modify the aircraft to parallel the main and auxiliary batteries during start sequences to prevent engine damage in austere environments. The Government considers Leonardo Service Bulletin SB 139-360 Rev C, Part II, (including Kit P/Ns 4G2430F00713) as the known baseline solution. Key requirements for the system include: System Functionality: Simultaneous utilization of main and auxiliary batteries during engine start sequences. Proposed solutions must either be the OEM kits or an equivalent FAA-approved modification that meets the exact same requirement. Airworthiness Support: The vendor must provide the necessary engineering data package to support a Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Supplemental Type Certificate (STC) and a military Engineering Change Proposal (ECP). Critical Exclusion (Batteries): The USAF currently possesses compatible Nickle-Cadmium 44 Ah Main and 27 Ah Auxiliary batteries.[CA1] [BA2] [JC3] Modification pricing must strictly exclude the physical batteries and include only the installation hardware (relays, brackets, wiring, consumables). Support & Documentation: The vendor must provide the necessary technical data package (e.g., flight manual supplements, wiring diagrams, structural data, and software integration files) associated with their kit to allow the Government to integrate the modification into baseline aircraft and training devices. 3. INSTRUCTION TO POTENTIAL RESPONDENTS Respondents are encouraged to provide comprehensive responses that demonstrate existing capability, supply chain stability, and technical support qualifications. Please structure your response to address the following sections: A. Company Information: Company Name, Address, CAGE Code, and Website URL. Point of Contact (Name, Title, Phone, Email). Business Size Status under NAICS Code 336413 (Aircraft Manufacturing), with a size standard of 1,500 employees. Please self-certify for all applicable categories: Small Business (Yes/No) Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB) (Yes/No) HUBZone Certified (Yes/No) Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) (Yes/No) Company Ownership (Domestic or Foreign-owned). Interest as Prime Contractor or Subcontractor. B. Technical Capability, Logistics, and Sustainment: Provide a detailed description of your proposed hardware kit (whether providing the OEM baseline or an equivalent solution). Describe the Size, Weight, Power, Cooling, and Center of Gravity (CG) impacts of the installation hardware (excluding the batteries). Detail your strategy for interfacing the physical relay with the aircraft's Operational Flight Program (OFP) and Crew Alerting System (CAS) to provide pilot advisories, fault alerts, and engine Full Authority Digital Engine Control (FADEC) interlocks.[JC4] If a physical switch or manual control is required for the activation of the proposed solution, the vendor must detail the strategy for aircraft modification, including the exact proposed placement of the interface to ensure in-flight aircrew accessibility. Provide engineering analysis or electrical modeling curves demonstrating the system's ability to maintain transient voltage above the engine hot-start threshold during a simulated start sequence at temperatures down to -40�C (-40�F). Provide proof of your company being part 145 certified. Sustainment & Tooling: Identify any proprietary or non-standard tooling required for installation. Identify strict shelf-life limitations or specialized storage/packing requirement for any kit consumables (e.g., adhesives, sealants). Confirm supply chain capability to provide individual replacement parts (relays, brackets) for long-term sustainment. Describe the technical data package provided with your kit and detail how your company will ensure the USAF Program Office receives future engineering revisions, safety notices, or updates related to this specific kit. Provide an impact analysis on how aircrew training syllabi and training devices (e.g., flight simulators, Weapons System Trainers, Cockpit Part Task Trainers, Operational Flight Trainers) will need to be updated. Acknowledge your ability to provide the necessary engineering artifacts required to support a Government CCB, ECP development, and TCTO generation. Facility Suitability: Describe the facility/depot where this installation would occur. Confirm that your facility meets the minimum footprint, tooling, and safety standards (e.g., specialized battery storage, hazardous material handling, and overhead clearance) required to perform the parallel battery kit installation. Throughput and Parallel Capacity: What is your maximum capacity for simultaneous (parallel) aircraft installations? Please detail how your facility layout and tooling availability support this throughput. C. Cost, Schedule, and Manpower: Provide a Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) cost estimate broken down in two parts: Non-Recurring Engineering (NRE): Electrical design, software/CAS integration, flight manual updates, and ECP/STC certification data package support, to include the engineering source data required for TCTO generation and Technical Order (TO) updates. Modification Kit & Field Installation: The per-aircraft cost to procure the physical hardware (excluding batteries) and perform the retrofit installation. Provide an estimated timeline for the development, testing, kit delivery lead times, and initial operational capability of the first modified aircraft. Validation of Maintenance Man-Hours (MMH): Respondents must name estimated MMH, and then clarify this estimate by addressing the following: The assumed environment/conditions for this estimate (e.g., controlled factory/depot environment vs. an operational flightline hangar). Active "touch-labor" hours vs. passive calendar/cure time, including whether the estimate assumes standard room-temperature or accelerated heat curing. Assumed crew size (single technician vs. multi-person). Inclusion or exclusion of post-installation testing and airworthiness sign-off time. Detail your available certified manpower (specifically avionics technicians and structural installers) to support the modification effort. Clarify if dedicated crews will be used for each aircraft, or if staff will be shared across multiple, parallel installation lines. Describe your crewing strategy for handling multiple, parallel aircraft modification lines (e.g., dedicated crews per aircraft vs. shared staff). D. Small Business Utilization: For Small Businesses: Describe how you will comply with FAR 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting, if this requirement is set-aside. For Large Businesses: Provide a realistic small business utilization target as a percentage of total contract value and explain your rationale. 4. RESPONSES AND COMMUNICATIONS Responses shall not e

title: Request for Information (RFI) for Joint Project Manager for Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Protection (JPM CBRN P) Chemically Protected Deployable Medical System (CP DEPMEDS)
description: **RFI extended to December 11th, 2026 Amendment posted to answer vendor questions This is a request for information (RFI) only for capabilities and experience which show potential for meeting the requirements described below. This is not a Request for Quotation (RFQ), Request for Proposal (RFP) or an Invitation for Bid (IFB). It is a market research tool being used to determine the availability and adequacy of potential sources for planning purposes only. Responses to this notice are not considered as offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of responses nor otherwise pay for the preparation of any information presented or the use of any such information. 1. Purpose The Joint Project Manager for Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear Protection (JPM CBRN P) is conducting a market survey to identify industry capabilities, experience, and potential approaches for serving as a Product Support Integrator (PSI) and material integration support for the Chemically Protected Deployable Medical System (CP DEPMEDS) Reconfiguration and Technology Refresh effort. The Government seeks a commercial partner capable of procuring and coordinating the delivery of commercially available components; receiving, tracking, and consolidating Government-sourced components; applying Item Unique Identification (IUID) markings as required; maintaining materiel accountability and readiness; conducting Preventative Maintenance, Checks and Services (PMCS) and Care of Supply in Storage (COSIS) as necessary, and delivering verified, complete component packages to Pine Bluff Arsenal (PBA) for final system integration, build completion, and packaging. This RFI is issued solely for planning and market-research purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation, request for proposal, commitment by the Government, or authorization to incur costs. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs associated with preparing or submitting a response. 2. Background CP DEPMEDS is a fielded CBRN protection system that supports Army Role 3 field-hospital operations. The program is executing a reconfiguration and technology-refresh effort using fielded, previously qualified, and commercially available components. The revised support concept under consideration would use a commercial PSI to integrate component procurement, Government-furnished or Government-sourced materiel coordination, traceability, IUID marking, and delivery to Pine Bluff Arsenal (PBA). PBA would retain responsibility for final assembly/integration of CP DEPMEDS sets, final packaging, associated Government acceptance activities, and delivery of sets to their fielding/final destination. 3. Scope of Information Requested The Government seeks information on industry capability to perform the following functions: A. Commercial Component Procurement Procure commercially available components identified by the Government. Conduct vendor management and order placement of components. Identify long-lead items, supply-chain constraints, discontinuance risks, and proposed alternate sources. Provide proposed substitutes only when specifically authorized by the Government. Manage warranties, vendor documentation, certificates of conformance, and commercial shipping documentation as applicable. B. Government Component Coordination Coordinate receipt, transfer, and consolidation of Government-sourced components from designated Government organizations, depots, supply activities, or other locations. Maintain accountability for Government-provided or Government-directed materiel while in contractor custody. Maintain COSIS to prevent environmental degradation, corrosion, and shelf life expiration of stored equipment and supplies. Reconcile shipping discrepancies, damaged materiel, shortages, overages, and documentation issues. Maintain traceability between each component, its source, and its assigned CP DEPMEDS configuration or set. Note: The contractor would not independently obligate Government funds or direct Government supply activities. The Government would retain authority for requisitions, funding, release, acceptance, and disposition decisions. C. IUID and Asset Identification Apply, validate, and document IUID markings for designated end items and components in accordance with Government-furnished requirements and applicable standards. Verify marking quality, placement, readability, and association with the correct item record. Maintain item-level records linking serial number, part number, National Stock Number, Unique Item Identifier, source, and destination. Provide electronic IUID and asset-accountability data deliverables in a Government-specified format. D. Materiel Receiving, Inspection, and Staging Receive and inspect commercial and Government-sourced components. Verify quantities, part numbers, serial numbers, condition, shelf life, and required documentation. Store and stage components in a manner that preserves condition, supports shelf-life management, and enables rapid consolidation into required delivery packages. Maintain COSIS to prevent environmental degradation, corrosion, and shelf life expiration of stored equipment and supplies. E. Kit Completion and Delivery to PBA Build component-level shipping packages in accordance with Government-approved bills of material, configuration lists, and delivery priorities. Conduct kit-completeness checks before shipment. Package, preserve, mark, and ship components to PBA in accordance with Government-approved shipping instructions. Provide advance-shipment notifications, packing lists, serial-number/IUID records, and discrepancy reports. If required, travel to PBA to help support the delivery and inventory of shipped equipment. F. Program Management and Reporting Maintain an integrated procurement and delivery schedule. Provide recurring status reports addressing procurement status, component availability, shortages, long-lead risks, delivery forecasts, IUID status, kit completion, and shipment status. Identify risks early and recommend mitigation actions, including alternate vendors, phased deliveries, or proposed substitutes. Participate in Government-led integrated product team meetings as required. 4. Desired Capabilities Respondents should describe experience performing comparable work involving: Multi-vendor procurement and materiel integration; Government-furnished property or Government-directed materiel; IUID marking, validation, and data management; Military logistics, asset accountability, and shipping documentation; Kitting, staging, packaging, preservation, and shipment of complex equipment; Supply-chain risk management and long-lead-item mitigation; CBRN, deployable medical, field-hospital, shelter, or comparable expeditionary equipment. (Note: This is desired experience but not required for response.) The Government is particularly interested in respondents able to manage multiple sources of supply and coordinate delivery of components to a Government integration location. 5. Industry Response Instructions Responses should not exceed [15] pages, excluding attachments. Include: Company Information: Name, UEI, CAGE code, business size, socioeconomic status, and points of contact. Relevant Experience: Up to three relevant efforts performed within the past five years. Technical Approach: Notional approach to commercial procurement, Government-component coordination, IUID, accountability, staging, kit verification, and delivery to PBA. Facilities and Workforce: Relevant facilities, quality systems, logistics staff, IUID capability, and geographic support model. Data and Reporting: Proposed methods for inventory visibility, serialized-item traceability, IUID data delivery, and Government status reporting. Risk Management: Principal risks, including vendor lead time, part obsolescence, Government materiel availability, configuration changes, and transportation de

description: Disclaimer: This notice is for informational purposes only. This is not a request for proposal or quote. It does not constitute a solicitation and shall not be construed as a commitment by the government or a guarantee that one will be issued in the future. Responses in any form are not offers and the government is under no obligation to award a contract as a result of this announcement. No funds are available to pay for preparation of responses to this announcement. Any information submitted by respondents is strictly voluntary. The Department of Justice (Department or DOJ) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to seek information regarding industry capabilities to provide modernization and enhancements to a 24/7 conferencing and communications center. Vendors should provide details on enhancing capabilities into a modern state-of-the-art facility suitable for executive level staff and their guests and increasing situational awareness capabilities. Vendors should also provide details on services they can provide for 24/7 operational centers. The DOJ is reviewing the marketplace to proactively examine all available options to ensure that the Department�s technology investments deliver maximum value, flexibility, and innovation today, and into the future. Project Name: Department of Justice Phase II Renovation Background: The space is a secure 24-hour facility operating in support of law enforcement and national security programs. The space is designed to function during routine operations and emergencies. The last renovations to the space were in 2006 and consisted of minor cosmetic improvements. The space needs major renovations to continue to provide the best service possible to the Departmental leadership. Objectives: The modernization encompasses the renovation and upgrade of the suite, which currently comprises three (3) conference rooms, one (1) watch floor, two (2) IT server rooms, two (2) restrooms, and one (1) storage room. The renovation shall deliver the following enhancements: upgrades to existing conference rooms to modern standards suitable for executive-level meetings and high-level briefings, modern design elements and finishes, renovation of the watch floor to support advanced situational awareness and real-time operational collaboration, and upgrades to all common areas and support spaces to contemporary standards while maintaining compliance with all security and operational requirements. Upon completion, the renovations shall provide a modern environment that is suitable for executive level staff and supports the Department�s mission. Miscellaneous Requirements: Security: 1. Contractors must be able to pass National Crime Information Center (NCIC) background check for building access. The space is a Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF), therefore no devices with Wi-Fi or Bluetooth, photography, and/or recording capabilities are permitted. 2. All visitors to the Restricted Area build site will be escorted/monitored by cleared personnel. Availability: The space is a 24/7 operation; however, work should be done after normal business hours (1800 � 0600) to limit disruptions to Department leadership. Compliance: 1. Intelligence Community Directive (ICD) 705; 2. ICD 705-1 Technical Specifications; and 3. TEMPEST Countermeasures. Tasks: Room 1: 1. Unclassified Telephone Security Group (TSG) 6 approved speaker phone 5. Hidden but easily accessible cable raceway; and 6. New executive level furniture to include credenza,, and end tables; and 7. TotalMass MassLoaded Vinyl (MLV) Barrier (sounds dampening material which meets Sound Transmission Class (STC) 50 sound attenuation requirements); and 8. Replace existing carpet with new carpet tiles (unique to AG Conference Room space) Room 2: 1. Modernized appearance with new drywall, fresh paint, and updated decorative lighting (sconces); and 2. Updated Department Wall Signage; and 3. Dedicated workspaces (2) which allow for up to four (4) enclaves, one (1) keyboard, one (1) mouse, two (2) monitors, and one (1) KVM; and 4. Additional seating along walls; and 5. New podium (reduced size to accommodate video wall) with three (3) JCON enclaves; and 6. TotalMass MLV Barrier (sounds dampening material which meets STC-50 sound attenuation requirements). Room 3: 1. Executive level conference table for up to six (6) people; and 2. New 60� credenza to accommodate IT equipment and wiring; and 3. One (1) desk with three (3) enclaves; and 4. Executive level chairs; and 5. Enhanced appearance with new drywall and fresh paint; and 6. Match carpet tiles to existing floor in the suite; and 7. New LED lighting and ceiling tiles; and 8. Two 75� 4k LED monitors. Room 4: 1. Collaborative layout desks for the Watch Officers; and 2. Dedicated workspace for the Lead Emergency Actions Specialist and Lead Telecommunication Specialist within the watch floor (Two Leads, Two Watch Officers); and 3. New 24/7 high durability desk chairs (5 chairs total); and 4. Printer Cove with three (3) printers (GFE); and 5. Built-in cabinetry for storage and binders; and 6. Additional desk for shared IT equipment (GFE) (LMR Radio, WashFax, Desktop VTC etc.); and 7. Zoned LED lighting with dimmer switch(s) compatible with watch environment; and 8. Hidden but easily accessible cable raceway; and 9. Dry Erase Magnetic Glass Board for planning; and 10. Privacy Smart Glass window between the Watch Room and the Situation Room 11. Adjustable temperature control for HVAC; and 12. Black 2x2 ceiling tiles; and 13. Remove or lower the existing raised floor for ADA compliance; and 14. New DOJ Signage; and 15. Six (6) Belkin 4:2 Display Port MultiClave Secure KVM. Lobby/Reception Area (Modernized Design and Functionality): 1. Fresh paint; and 2. Additional seating; and 3. Improved LED signage throughout; and 4. New Department of Justice Signage outside SCIF; and 5. Recessed cell phone lockers outside of the SCIF. Modernizing the space into a state-of-the-art communications and meeting hub will provide Cabinet-level officials and senior managers with a secure, resilient, and highly adaptable environment for decision-making, collaboration, and organizational coordination. The existing space can be transformed from a primarily operational command function into a multi-functional executive hub capable of supporting high-level meetings, crisis response, strategic communications, and hybrid collaboration. V. m. § 100 Abs. 1 Nr.1 und 102 Abs. 4 GWB mit Betriebsaufnahme zum 01.01.2028 zu vergeben. Der Verkehrsverbund Rhein-Neckar GmbH — B1 3-5, 68159 Mannheim — führt als Vergabestelle die Vergabe im Namen der Stadtverkehr Bad Mergentheim durch. Folgende Regelungen zur Tariftreue und Sozialstandards sind zur Sicherung der Betriebsqualität Teil der ausreichenden Verkehrsbedienung: Aufgrund der Arbeitsmarktsituation in der Metropolregion Rhein-Neckar und der Wirtschaftsregionen Vorderpfalz und Rheinhessen wird der künftige Betreiber verpflichtet, seinen Beschäftigten zur Sicherung einer aus-reichenden Qualifikation des Fahrpersonals bei der Ausführung der Leistung mindestens gemäß LTMG entsprechend der repräsentativ erklärten Tarifverträgen festgelegte Entgelt zu zahlen sowie die in diesen Tarifverträgen festgelegten Arbeitsbedingungen zu garantieren. Weitere Vorgaben finden Sie unter: https://www.landesrecht-bw.de/jportal/portal/page/bsbawueprod.psml/action/portlets.jw.MainAction? eventSubmit_doNavigate=searchInSubtreeTOC&showdoccase=1&doc.id=jlr- Tarift_MindLohnGBWpP8. Diese Verpflichtung gilt für die gesamte Laufzeit des neuen Vertragszeitraumes dynamisch, also stets mit Bezug auf die jeweils noch erfolgenden Anpassungen der Tarifverträge in der Zukunft. Erfolgt der Einsatz von Subunternehmern, haben diese ebenfalls die Einhaltung dieser Verpflichtungen zu garantieren. Zusätzlich zu den tarifvertraglich zu garantierenden Sozialstandards gelten für alle eingesetzten Fahrerinnen und Fahrer folgende Bedingungen zu Lenkzeitunterbrechungen und Pausen: Tarifvertraglich nicht als Arbeitszeit geltende Lenkzeitunterbrechungen und Pausen dürfen je Schichtmaximal 60 Minuten betragen. Überschreiten die Lenkzeitunterbrechungen und Pausen diese Grenze, sind die 60-Minuten-Grenze überschreitenden Zeiten der Arbeitsunterbrechungen der Arbeitszeit zuzurechnen. Als echte, nicht zu vergütende Freizeit im Sinne eines geteilten Dienstes zählt eine einmalige Arbeitsunterbrechung je Schicht von mind. 2 Std, die am Wohnort (Stadtteil) des Mitarbeiters oder an einem Betriebsstandort mit adäquaten Sozialräumen beginnen und enden. Die Vorhaltung von Sozialräumen ist in diesem Zusammenhang nicht relevant, sofern die Arbeitsunterbrechung länger als 4 Std dauert. Folgende Regelungen zur Personalübernahme sind ebenfalls zur Sicherung der Betriebsqualität Teil der ausreichenden Verkehrsbedienung: Die Bieter verpflichten sich im Rahmen ihres Angebotes, denjenigen Fahrer/innen einen Arbeitsvertrag anzubieten, die während der Vergabe im Betrieb des Altbetreibers des Linienbündels mindestens mit 70 % der regulären Arbeitszeit eingesetzt sind und die zum Zeitpunkt der Inbetriebnahme einen gültigen Arbeitsvertrag mit dem Altbetreiber vorweisen können. Der neue Arbeitsvertrag ist unbefristet und ohne Probezeit abzuschließen. Grundlage des Einstellungsangebotes müssen die im Unternehmen des Konzessionsnehmers für die übrige Belegschaft geltenden tarifvertraglichen und in Betriebsvereinbarungen geregelten Konditionen sein. Sofern der im übernehmenden Unternehmen praktizierte Tarifvertrag die Höhe des Entgeltes sowie die Zahl der Urlaubstage von der Dauer der Betriebszugehörigkeit abhängig gestaltet, muss der neue Anstellungsvertrag vorsehen, dass die Betriebszugehörigkeit beim Altbetreiber im Rahmen der entgeltlichen Eingruppierung und Urlaubsgewährung wie eine Betriebszugehörigkeit im übernehmenden Unternehmen gewertet wird.

title: UVT - Overscenemaskineri – Hovedsal, DKS-sal og Multirom
description: Stiftelsen Unge Viken Teater anskaffer komplett overscenemaskineri til Hovedsal, DKS-sal og Multirom i Kirkegata 11, 2000 Lillestrøm. Leveransen omfatter prosjektering, fabrikasjon, levering, montasje, styringssystemer, kabling for maskinfunksjoner, innregulering, prøving, dokumentasjon og opplæring. Hovedsal: 14 motoriserte trekk og 3 faste trekk, med nyttelast 300 daN (3,00 kN) per trekk. Motoriserte trekk skal holde og bevege scenisk last over personer som selvstendige maskinakser med hver sin last, UC3. Styresystemet skal støtte cues/scener og ivareta hovedleveransens UC3-bruk etter H-09. Tillatte driftsfunksjoner skal følge det tilkoblede maskineriets bruksområde. DKS-sal: 12 motortaljer à 500 kg og tre trosserammer à 7 000 × 2 500 mm. Multirom: 8 motortaljer à 500 kg og to trosserammer, 5 750 × 4 500 mm og 5 500 × 4 500 mm. Hver ramme løftes av fire taljer som koordinert gruppe for UC2. Heving og senking skjer med avsperret og tomt fareområde. Statisk lastholding over personer skal være dokumentert for maskineriets normale lastbærende system i alle salene. Opsjoner omfatter høyere brukskategorier, tre ekstra motoriserte trekk i Hovedsal, pantografer for kabelføring til alle tre trosserammer i DKS-sal og begge trosserammer i Multirom, samt ti flyttbare kabeltrommelenheter med 230 V énfase og Cat.5e til Hovedsalen. Opsjoner beskrives og prises separat etter O-01–O-08, inklusive kombinasjonstillegg O-01T og O-02T. Veiledende anslag for hovedleveransen inklusive fellesytelser: Hovedsal 2 000 000 kroner, DKS-sal 950 000 kroner og Multirom 700 000 kroner; samlet 3 650 000 kroner eks. mva. Tilbudet og opsjonene prises etter prisskjemaet. Det inngås én samlet varekontrakt etter NS 8407:2011 med tilpasningene i konkurransegrunnlaget. Tildeling skjer etter pris 35 %, kvalitet 35 % og klima og miljø – levetid og ressursbruk 30 %. Tidligste montasjestart er 01.02.2027. Hovedleveransen og utløste opsjoner O-01–O-05 og O-08 skal være ferdige og klare til overtakelse senest 31.03.2027. Pantografopsjonene O-06 og O-07 kan ettermonteres og skal være ferdige senest 30.06.2027. Prisevalueringen omfatter P-01–P-09 + O-06 + O-07 + O-08. Fullstendige krav fremgår av konkurransegrunnlag versjon 1.0, datert 11.11.2026, med kravbesvarelse, prisskjema og A20-01 revisjon 01.

Der Auftragnehmer hat die Leistungen während der Laufzeit der Rahmenvereinbarung nach den bei Abruf der Einzelverträge (Jahres-Abrufe) geltenden anerkannten Regeln der Technik zu erbringen. Soweit möglich, steht dem Auftraggeber in diesem Fall ein Wahlrecht zu, welche Leistungsvarianten im Rahmen des Einzelvertrages ausgeführt werden sollen. Hierdurch entstehende Mehrkosten werden vom Auftraggeber getragen. Der Auftragnehmer hat in jedem Fall die im Leistungsverzeichnis (Kapitel 4.0 ) zugesagten Kriterien zu erfüllen. Die Rahmenvereinbarung begründet keine Abnahme- und Leistungsverpflichtungen. title: Denmark – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – Rammeaftale for support og videreudvikling af Byggesag, Budget og Aftalesystem (BBA)
description: Bygningsstyrelsen ønsker at indgå en rammeaftale med én (1) leverandør til support og videreudvikling af fagsystemet Byggesag, Budget og Aftalesystem (herefter ”BBA”). Bygningsstyrelsen, som er ejendomsvirksomhed og bygherre for staten og universiteterne, kan gøre brug af rammeaftalen. BBA anvendes til økonomistyring af Bygningsstyrelsens bygge-, vedligeholdelses- og kunstprojekter. Systemet blev taget i brug i 2024 og er i stabil drift. Bygningsstyrelsen anser BBA for et forretningskritisk system. BBA er baseret på Navision Stat v.11.2 (ØSC Navision), som ejes og videreudvikles af Øko-nomistyrelsen på basis af Microsoft Dynamics NAV. I efteråret 2026 overgår BBA til Driftsmodel 1A (Applikationsdrift) i Statens IT, hvor Bygningsstyrelsen ejer og er ansvarlig for udvikling og ændringer af BBA, mens Statens IT har driftsansvar for BBA, middleware, operativsystem og underliggende driftsinfrastruktur. For at sikre relevans og anvendelighed vil der jævnligt være behov for videreudvikling og funktionelt vedligehold af BBA. En aktuel og kritisk udviklingsopgave vedrører Økonomistyrelsens opgradering af Navision Stat til Microsoft Business Central, som får afledte konsekvenser for BBA i 2027. Herudover er der i mindre omfang behov for ad hoc support til mindre vedligeholdelsesopgaver i den eksisterende konfiguration, herunder eksempelvis fejlrettelse vedrørende forbrugsopgørelser på enkelte byggesager. Der henvises til udbudsmaterialet. Udbudsbetingelserne indeholder en nærmere beskrivelse af opgaven og udbudsforløbet, og det øvrige materiale indeholder en beskrivelse af opgavens omfang.

description: Beschreibung der Leistung: Das Bezirksamt Hamburg-Mitte entwickelt als Schlüsselprojekt der RISE-Gebietsentwicklung Billstedt/Horn das ehemalige Jugend-Europahaus als neues “Haus im Blohms Park” mit Angeboten zur Gesundheitsvorsorge, einem kleinen Park-Café und Angeboten für unterstützungsbedürftige junge Menschen. title: Germany – Architectural and related services – Stadt Schrobenhausen | Stadthalle VgV-Verfahren mit Teilnahmewettbewerb nach §17 VgV und Lösungsvorschlägen nach § 76 Abs. 2 VgV
description: Im Rahmen eines EU-weiten Vergabeverfahrens mit Mehrfachbeauftragung von Lösungsansätzen soll eine belastbare Entscheidungsgrundlage für die künftige Entwicklung der Stadthalle in Schrobenhausen erarbeitet werden. Die unmittelbar neben dem Zentralen Omnibusbahnhof (ZOB) gelegene Stadthalle wurde im Jahr 1996 eröffnet und stellte über viele Jahre einen bedeutenden Veranstaltungsort für kulturelle, sportliche und gesellschaftliche Ereignisse dar. Aufgrund erheblicher brandschutztechnischer Defizite kann das Gebäude jedoch seit mehreren Jahren nicht mehr genutzt werden. Es liegen bereits erste Machbarkeitsstudien und Untersuchungen für eine Sanierung der bestehenden Halle wie auch Ersatzneubau vor. Die Stadt Schrobenhausen benötigt eine öffentliche Veranstaltungs- und Begegnungsstätte, mit einer Kapazität von ca. 470 (für Bestandssanierung) bis 600 Sitzplätzen (für Neubau). Aufgrund der bestehenden Förderkulissen und der zu betrachtenden Nachhaltigkeit ist eine Bestandssanierung zu betrachten. Eine Reduzierung der Sitzplatzkapazität um bis zu 130 Plätze kann daher in Betracht gezogen werden, sofern dies zur Ermöglichung bzw. Umsetzung der Sanierungsmaßnahmen erforderlich ist. Der Bereich um die Stadthalle soll in die aktuellen Planungen zu Landesgartenschau 2031 mit neuer Stadtterrasse und Zugang zur Paar integriert werden. Gegenstand der Aufgabenstellung sind realisierbare Lösungen für eine Bestandssanierung, mit Erweiterung oder Ersatzneubau der Stadthalle unter Berücksichtigung funktionaler, wirtschaftlicher und hochwasserschutzrechtlicher Anforderungen. Die Gesamtlösung soll eine langfristig tragfähige, funktional und gestalterisch hochwertige und wirtschaftlich umsetzbare Perspektive für die Stadthalle als Veranstaltungshalle mit Foyer, Gastrobereich (für den Betrieb den Betrieb während Veranstaltungen), Bühne und Funktionsräumen für den Veranstaltungsbetrieb inkl. teilbarer Saal, für Nebenräume aufzeigen. Die veranschlagten Gesamtkosten (KG 300-400) für die Baumaßnahme Stadthalle liegen bei ca. 9 Mio.€ Nettobaukosten. Die gesamten Kosten incl. MwSt. sollen bei max. 14,65 Mio.€ liegen.

description: Die Jüdische Gemeinde in Hamburg beabsichtigt die Wiedererrichtung der im Jahr 1938 zerstörten historischen Bornplatzsynagoge am Joseph-Carlebach-Platz im Hamburger Grindelviertel. Das Vorhaben knüpft an die historische, religiöse und städtebauliche Bedeutung des Ortes an und verfolgt das Ziel, einen zentralen Ort jüdischen Glaubens, jüdischer Kultur und jüdischen Gemeindelebens im Stadtraum Hamburgs wieder sichtbar und erlebbar zu machen. Auf Grundlage einer Machbarkeitsstudie sowie eines unterdessen abgeschlossenen nicht-offenen, zweiphasigen hochbaulich-freiraumplanerischen Realisierungswettbewerbs wird das Projekt im Sinne einer kritischen Rekonstruktion weiterentwickelt. Die Kubatur und äußere Erscheinung des historischen Hauptbaukörpers sollen in Anlehnung an den 1906 errichteten Vorgängerbau wiederhergestellt werden, während die innere Organisation, technische Ausstattung und Sicherheitskonzeption zeitgemäßen funktionalen, gesellschaftlichen und nachhaltigen Anforderungen folgen. Das Projekt umfasst den Neubau einer orthodoxen Synagoge als Hauptbaukörper, ergänzende Gemeinde-, Bildungs- und Verwaltungsbereiche sowie einen zusätzlichen liberalen Synagogenraum. Bestandteil des Vorhabens ist zudem die Neugestaltung der umgebenden Freiräume im Zusammenspiel mit dem Grindelhof sowie dem Allende- und Joseph-Carlebach-Platz. Aufgrund der herausragenden städtebaulichen, historischen und gesellschaftlichen Bedeutung des Ortes sowie der besonderen Sicherheitsrelevanz erfordert das Vorhaben eine integrierte und besonders enge Koordination mit allen Projektbeteiligten und Belange dieses Projektes.

title: Germany – Business and management consultancy services – Betrieb und Weiterentwicklung des nordrhein-westfälischen Kompetenzzentrums für Cybersicherheit in der Wirtschaft "DIGITAL.SICHER.NRW"
description: Die fortschreitende Digitalisierung und Vernetzung von Wirtschaft und Gesellschaft eröffnet erhebliche Chancen, erhöht zugleich jedoch die Abhängigkeit von funktionsfähigen und sicheren digitalen Strukturen. Cyberangriffe und insbesondere Ransomware können zu erheblichen wirtschaftlichen Schäden, Betriebsunterbrechungen, Datenabflüssen und Reputationsverlusten führen. Technologische Entwicklungen wie KI-gestützte Angriffsmethoden sowie geopolitisch motivierte und staatlich gesteuerte Aktivitäten verschärfen die Bedrohungslage zusätzlich. Dies betrifft insbesondere Unternehmen in technologieintensiven, sicherheitsrelevanten und versorgungskritischen Wertschöpfungs- und Lieferketten. Cybersicherheit und Resilienz dienen daher auch dem Erhalt der Funktions-, Produktions- und Lieferfähigkeit der Wirtschaft in Nordrhein-Westfalen. Insbesondere kleine und mittlere Unternehmen (KMU) stehen dabei vor besonderen Herausforderungen. Ihnen fehlen häufig personelle und finanzielle Ressourcen, spezialisierte Fachkräfte und etablierte Sicherheitsprozesse. Gleichzeitig nehmen sie als spezialisierte Anbieter und Zulieferer vielfach eine wichtige Rolle innerhalb regionaler und überregionaler Wertschöpfungsstrukturen ein. Unter teils hohem Kosten- und Wettbewerbsdruck werden Investitionen in Cybersicherheit dennoch häufig zu spät oder nicht ausreichend priorisiert. Dabei können bereits grundlegende organisatorische und technische Maßnahmen die Widerstandsfähigkeit eines Unternehmens deutlich erhöhen. Hinzu kommt, dass staatliche oder technisch geprägte Informationsangebote von KMU teilweise als zu abstrakt, zu komplex oder zu wenig auf ihre betriebliche Praxis zugeschnitten wahrgenommen werden. Das Land Nordrhein-Westfalen unterstützt Unternehmen daher mit DIGITAL.SICHER.NRW, einem etablierten Kompetenzzentrum für Cybersicherheit in der Wirtschaft. Ziel ist es, Unternehmen - insbesondere KMU - praxisnah dazu zu befähigen, Cyberrisiken zu erkennen, angemessen zu priorisieren und durch umsetzbare Maßnahmen wirksam zu reduzieren. Das Kompetenzzentrum verfolgt dabei den Grundsatz der "Hilfe zur Selbsthilfe" und ist eine neutrale, vertrauenswürdige und regional wirksame Schnittstelle zwischen vorhandenem Sicherheitswissen und der betrieblichen Praxis. Es ergänzt bestehende Strukturen und Angebote des Bundes und des Landes, indem es Informationen verständlich aufbereitet, konkrete Umsetzungsimpulse vermittelt, regionale Zugänge schafft und wirtschaftsnahe Multiplikatoren einbindet. Über die unmittelbare Unterstützung von Unternehmen hinaus verfolgt das Kompetenzzentrum das Ziel, relevante Akteure im Themenfeld Cybersicherheit in Nordrhein-Westfalen zu vernetzen und den Wissenstransfer aus Wissenschaft und Forschung in die wirtschaftliche Praxis zu fördern. DIGITAL.SICHER.NRW besteht seit 2021. Der Vertrag mit dem bisherigen Dienstleister endet am 31.12.2026. Im Rahmen des Offenen Verfahrens wird ein Auftragnehmer gesucht, der die Arbeit des Kompetenzzentrums für Cybersicherheit in der Wirtschaft in den kommenden Jahren fortführt und weiterentwickelt. Inhaltliche Schwerpunkte der kommenden Vertragslaufzeit bilden insbesondere die Prävention und Bewältigung von Ransomware-Angriffen, die praxisnahe Aufbereitung aktueller und sich wandelnder Bedrohungen sowie die Berücksichtigung besonderer Bedarfe von KMU in technologieintensiven, sicherheitsrelevanten und versorgungskritischen Wertschöpfungs- und Lieferketten. Die grundlegende Ausrichtung des Kompetenzzentrums auf präventive, leicht zugängliche Unterstützung, die Stärkung der Resilienz und die Befähigung zur Selbsthilfe bleibt hiervon unberührt.

title: Sweden – Building construction work – Ombyggnation Restadgård hus 1, 19 och 21
description: Migrationsverket är den myndighet i Sverige som prövar ansökningar från personer som vill bosätta sig i Sverige, komma på besök, arbeta eller studera i Sverige, söka skydd undan förföljelse eller ha svenskt medborgarskap. Migrationsverket erbjuder asylsökande boende och pengar till mat under den tiden de väntar på besked i asylärendet. När en asylsökande har fått sitt tillstånd att stanna i Sverige betalar Migrationsverket ut statlig ersättning till kommuner och regioner. Om en asylsökande får avslag på sin ansökan är Migrationsverket aktivt i arbetet med att få personen att lämna Sverige. Migrationsverket har boenden för asylsökande i egen regi. Migrationsverket har sitt säte i Norrköping, men har verksamhet över hela landet. Ytterligare information kan erhållas på vår hemsida www.migrationsverket.se (http://www.migrationsverket.se) Restad gård i Vänersborg är ett av Sveriges största asylboende. Migrationsverket har administrativ verksamhet på plats och det finns flera frivilligorganisationer som bedriver aktiviteter för våra boende. Entreprenaden omfattar att på totalentreprenad utföra ombyggnad av Hus 1, 19 och 21. I entreprenaden ingår nybyggnation av ett (1) stycken Miljöhus Laddning. Projektet ”Ombyggnation Restad gård, hus 1, 19 och 21” genomförs som en del av kraftsamlingsområde ”Sammanhållet mottagningssystem” genom EU:s migrations och asylpakt. Ett reformerat mottagningssystem där asylsökande vistas på mottagningscenter eller återvändandecenter ska bidra till att uppfylla regeringens mål om en effektivare asylprocess och ett effektivare återvändande.

description: This is a notification of DLA Weapons Support � Richmond�s intention to bundle F135 propulsion system sustainment requirements into a long-term holistic contract. title: USACE Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center Scope Dredge to Budget Contract
description: W912PM27RA006 Intent to Consolidate Notice The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center requires a contract to perform maintenance dredging of seven (7) dredging projects. The areas of consideration for these dredging services are Galveston Harbor & Channel, Houston Ship Channel, Texas City Ship Channel, Freeport Harbor, Matagorda Ship Channel, Corpus Christi Ship Channel, and Brazos Island Harbor located in Texas. In accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 7.107-3, the Government intends to consolidate seven (7) contracts for maintenance dredging of Galveston Harbor & Channel, Houston Ship Channel, Texas City Ship Channel, Freeport Harbor, Matagorda Ship Channel, Corpus Christi Ship Channel, and Brazos Island Harbor performed by a large business. The consolidated effort will be solicited as unrestricted. The consolidation of the seven (7) identified projects is in the best interest of the Government. This consolidation meets the requirements of RFO 7.107 and the benefits of the consolidated acquisition would substantially exceed the benefits that would be derived from an alternative approach. Therefore, the Government found that consolidation is necessary and justified and shall be available for seven days prior to the release of the solicitation for this requirement. The solicitation is anticipated for release on or around 19 November 2026.

description: See attached. Limited Sources FAR GSAR 538.7104-3(b)(1)(ii) (and FAR 8.401(b) This justification is for the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC), Office of Procurement Services. CPSC awarded 61320627F0007 to EMCOR Government Services, on a sole-source basis for specialized office renovations. CPSC requires specialized office renovations in the U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO) building. The total estimated value of the award is $436,996.41 which includes the necessary renovations to prepare offices for employees. Only one source is capable of providing the supplies or services required, following procedures would result in unacceptable delays. EMCOR is the GSA contractor that provides renovations to the GAO building. They are contracted to complete renovations. The contracting officer has determined that the order represents the best value consistent with 538.7104-3(b)(1)(ii). The price is deemed fair and reasonable based on Federal Supply Schedule Contract: 47QSHA19D0044 In accordance with FAR 8.404(d), the General Services Administration (GSA) has already determined the prices of supplies and fixed-price services under Federal Supply Schedule contracts to be fair and reasonable. This justification will be posted to SAM.gov within 14 days of award. The requirement cannot be modified to enhance competition, because the proposed contractor is the only one who can provide the renovations. The contracting officer certifies that the justification is accurate and complete to the best of the contracting officer�s knowledge and belief. Technical personnel who provided supporting data, which forms the basis for this justification have certified that the information is complete and accurate. The contracting officer has determined that the circumstances at FAR 538.7104-3(b)(1)(ii) apply to this acquisition.

title: Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Multiple Award Task Order Contracts (MATOC) for Design-Build (DB) Construction in Support of Defense Health Agency (DHA)
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Little Rock District (CESWL) announces its intent to solicit for an Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ), Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) for Design Build (DB) Construction Services in support of the Defense Health Agencys (DHA) Sustainment, Restoration, and Modernization (SRM) program.The Product Service Code is Z2DA (Repair or Alteration of Hospitals and Infirmaries), and the NAICS Code is 236220 (Commercial and Institutional Building Construction), with a size standard of $45 million.The scope of work for the resultant contracts will primarily be associated with the design, renovation/alteration of existing active medical facilities, but may also include major repair and new construction. Work may include restoration or modernization of hospitals, clinics, medical administration buildings, ambulatory health facilities, medical warehouses, medical labs, biological engineering labs, dental clinics, veterinary clinics, wellness centers, and any other buildings connected to or associated with the operations of Defense Health Agency (DHA) supported facilities. Required Contract Performance is within the continental United States (CONUS), Alaska and Hawaii (OCONUS), and US Territories with a potential for contracts to serve a certain region. The majority of work will be conducted in active healthcare facilities requiring multi-phase transitions of clinics and other operations. Experience and staffing for these types of projects is a requirement. Patient care and patient/staff safety in occupied space is paramount in design and construction. Compliance with all related governmental and non-governmental design and construction requirements is to be expected. Infection control in design and procedures during construction is paramount.Work may include, but is not limited to restoration and/or modernization of all aspects of heating ventilation, air conditioning and refrigeration (HVAC-R) systems, plumbing systems, medical gas and vacuum systems, building envelope, roofing systems, anti-terrorism/force protection (ATFP) features, electrical systems, elevators, fire protection, interior renovations, wayfinding and signage, and exterior site and systems work such as utilities infrastructure, roadways, sidewalks, parking lots, landscaping, irrigation, etc. Work may also include providing transition services, and facility furniture, fixtures and equipment. Transition services include the planning and move of occupants, existing property, and associated services. Facility furniture, fixtures and equipment includes items such as casework, systems furniture, cubicle partitions, seating and desking, patient room furniture, artwork, and medical equipment.Under this contract the contractor must provide all necessary labor, material, supervision, and equipment for the design, construction, repair, and/or alteration to sustain, restore, and or modernize these facilities using Military Construction (MILCON) and Operations and Maintenance (O and M) processes. The contractor shall have experience in utilizing performance based requirements, where the customer identifies the objectives (desired result) and the constraints (code/criteria/standards) and the contractor is responsible for determining the means and methods to achieving the desired result. Any resultant contracts will be for a base period of five (5) years, with no option periods. Each contract awarded under the DB MATOC will share the total contract capacity estimated at $250 million over the five (5) year period. The estimated The minimum size of a task order awarded against this MATOC is $300,000, while the maximum size is $20M. Individual task orders will be competed among all MATOC base contract awardees. Firms must have ability to perform up to five (5) task orders simultaneously. The Government has a target of six (6) contractors.Small Businesses and 8(a) participants are reminded under FAR 52.219-14(e), Limitations on Subcontracting, that they will not pay more than 85 percent of the amount paid by the Government for contract performance, excluding the cost of materials, to subcontractors that are not similarly situated entities. Any work that a similarly situated entity further subcontracts will count towards the prime contractors 85 percent subcontract amount that cannot be exceeded.The acquisition will be advertised as a Total Small Business Set-Aside.The evaluation and selection of awardees for the MATOC will be conducted in accordance with FAR Part 15 ? Contracting by Negotiation, and FAR Part 36.3 - Two-Phase DB Selection Procedures. Awardees will be selected based on demonstrated technical competence and qualifications. A selection process will be used in accordance with FAR Part 15, Best Value trade-off Evaluation. The Government will evaluate performance capability in accordance with criteria described in the solicitation documents.The Government will post the solicitation and all subsequent amendments to the Government-Wide Point of Entry (GPE) System of Award Management (SAM) and the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) Web Site http://www.sam.gov and www.piee.eb.mil. The offeror is solely responsible to obtain this solicitation and any subsequent amendments through these websites. Offerors are encouraged to visit the websites and become familiar with content and functionality prior to the solicitation issue date. Prospective Offerors must provide all information necessary to register for systems access and to receive posting notifications. Offerors must be registered and have an active, valid registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) database (https://www.sam.gov)and the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment Solicitation Module (PIEE). Offerors must also have a NIST Score recorded in PIEE to be eligible for award (https://piee.eb.mil/, to access SPRS/NIST Score). Anticipated solicitation issuance date is on or about 23 Dec 2024, and the estimated proposal due date will be on or about 05-Jan-2026. The proximity date of award is anticipated around 15-Jan-2027.

title: Sweden – Refuse disposal and treatment – Behandling av utsorterat matavfall 2027
description: Syfte Upphandlingens syfte är att säkerställa beställarnas behov av behandling av biologiskt lättnedbrytbart avfall under avtalstiden. En målsättning för beställarna är att upphandlingen ska bidra till minskad miljöbelastning inom avfallssektorn. Omfattning Med matavfall avses i detta kontrakt biologiskt nedbrytbart köks- och livsmedelsavfall enligt avfallsförordningen (2020:614). Anbudsgivaren ska hantera avfallet i enlighet med gällande krav på utsortering och separat insamling av bioavfall enligt avfallsförordningen och de fraktionsindelningar som där anges. Matavfallet ska hållas åtskilt från övriga bioavfallsfraktioner, exempelvis park- och trädgårdsavfall (exklusive fallfrukt), om inte annat överenskommits. Uppdraget omfattar mottagning, eventuell omlastning samt mellanlagring och biologisk behandling av biologiskt avfall, så kallat matavfall, från hushåll och verksamheter, pumpbart matavfall samt fallfrukt från hushåll insamlat från Nacka kommun, Värmdö kommun och Tyresö kommun. Den biologiska behandlingen ska bestå av rötning i rötningsanläggning för framställning av biogas och biogödsel. Biogödseln ska återföras till jordbruk/skogsbruk och ska vara certifierad enligt SPCR 120 Certifieringsregler för biogödsel, eller likvärdigt certifieringssystem, i den utgåva som gäller vid respektive tillfälle. I uppdraget ingår inte transport av matavfallet då transporten kommer att skötas av respektive beställares entreprenör, såvida inte behandlingsanläggningens placering kräver omlastning från respektive beställare.

title: Fiber Dial Room Refurbishment
description: INTRODUCTION Battelle Energy Alliance, LLC (BEA) Management & Operating Contractor of the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) owned Idaho National Laboratory (INL), is seeking an Expression of Interest (EOI) from qualified vendors to provide refurbishment services for the Fiber Dial Room and implement point-to-point fiber connectivity upgrades. This initiative supports BEA�s commitment to maintaining robust and reliable communications infrastructure across INL facilities. BACKGROUND The Fiber Dial Room requires refurbishment and modernization to support enhanced fiber optic connectivity and point-to-point communication capabilities. The scope of work may include the following: Remove legacy abandoned communication cables around the plant. Refurbishment of several Fiber Dial Rooms around TAN, including structural and environmental improvements and replacement of hardware. Installation and testing of new fiber and communications. Installation and configuration of point-to-point fiber connections. Integration with existing network infrastructure and systems. Compliance with DOE cybersecurity, safety, and operational standards. Testing and documentation to ensure full functionality and reliability. INL is a U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) national laboratory dedicated to nuclear energy, national security, and clean energy innovation. INL is operated under a management and operating contract with the Department of Energy and as such, the Davis-Bacon Act applies for contracts in excess of $2,000 for the construction, alteration, or repair (including painting and decorating) of buildings or works at INL. Construction work at the laboratory Site covered under the Davis-Bacon Act is additionally subject to the INL Site Stabilization Agreement (SSA). These Site areas include all areas within the 890-square mile boundary, including the Material and Fuels Complex, Central Facilities Area, Advanced Test Reactor, Radioactive Waste Management Complex, and Specific Manufacturing Capability. The agreement is between signatory contractors and labor unions performing such work. Information regarding the INL Site Stabilization Agreement is available from the Site Labor Coordinator at (208) 524-4404 or at lance@sitelabor.org. Construction work performed at Idaho Falls facilities is not subject to these agreements. PROCESS This EOI is the first step in identifying interested and qualified vendors. Responses may be used to inform the development of a formal solicitation list. Selected vendors may be invited to participate in a Request for Proposal (RFP) process for award consideration. SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS Interested vendors should submit an Expression of Interest that includes the following: Company name and point of contact Description of relevant fiber installation and refurbishment capabilities and experience NAICS codes and business size classification Any existing DOE or federal contracting experience (if applicable) Deadline for submission: December 11, 2026 Submit to: Chase.Egbert@inl.gov Only select respondents, as determined by BEA, will receive an invitation to participate in the anticipated RFP solicitation. PROPRIETARY INFORMATION Because information received in response to this EOI may be business sensitive or proprietary to the responding party, respondents must mark information in their responses accordingly.
